title: TinyForge: A Design Space Exploration to Advance Energy and Silicon Area Trade-offs in tinyML Compute Architectures with Custom Latch Arrays
problem: Custom hardware for tinyML must optimize the trade-offs between energy consumption, silicon area, and performance for small neural networks (50-500 KB) running at low frequencies (1-100 MHz) on resource-constrained IoT devices. Existing synthesized implementations waste significant area and energy through inefficient memory hierarchies and compute approaches.
motivation: Custom hardware tailored for tinyML can dramatically reduce energy consumption and silicon area compared to general-purpose approaches, enabling efficient deployment of neural networks on resource-constrained IoT devices.
method: TinyForge introduces a custom latch array integrated with compute memory fabric achieving 8 μm²/B density and 11 fJ/B read energy. The framework uses bit-serial instead of bit-parallel compute and optimizes systolic vs. combinational scaling in 2D arrays. TinyForge comprises parameterized templates for memory and compute fabric, power/area/latency estimators, a dataflow optimizer for workload scheduling, and a genetic algorithm performing multi-objective optimization to find Pareto-optimal architectures.
key_novelty: Custom latch arrays integrated with compute memory fabric that achieve unprecedented density and energy efficiency while enabling dataflows that eliminate activation buffer requirements.
contributions: Custom latch array architecture achieving 7x better density and 5x better read energy than synthesized implementations
Design space exploration framework (tinyForge) with parameterized templates and genetic algorithm-based multi-objective optimization
Bit-serial compute approach reducing area by 4.8x and multiply-accumulate energy by 2.3x compared to bit-parallel
Demonstration of 1.8x energy reduction, 2.2x latency reduction, and 3.7x area reduction on MLPerf Tiny and BERT-Tiny workloads

metrics.energy: 1.8x energy reduction per inference; 7.5x with on-chip weight storage vs off-chip
metrics.area: 3.7x silicon area reduction; 4.8x reduction from bit-serial compute
metrics.other: 8 μm²/B density (7x better), 11 fJ/B read energy (5x better) vs synthesized implementations

limitations: Not discussed in the abstract; evaluation limited to MLPerf Tiny and BERT-Tiny workloads.
primary_theme: Energy-efficient tinyML hardware with custom memory-compute integration
